19.05.2023 (Clause 31) AWARD 1.
This is a claim petition U/s 166 read with Section 140 of The Motor Vehicle's Act, 1988, filed by petitioners.

The facts of the case are that on 23.01.2018 at 17.30 hrs,at Red light, Sector04 and 12,
Dwarka New Delhi , a car bearing No. DL3CCF1319 being driven by respondent No.1 came at a very high speed, in negligent manner and hit the cyclist ( deceased).
As a result of this impact the deceased received injuries.

The deceased was taken to Ayushman Hospital where he was declared as brought dead vide MLC No.4694/2018 dated 23.01.2018.
2.

The present application/claim petition has been filed contending that said accident took place,
due to rash and negligent driving by (respondent no.1/ Driver) who was driving Car No. DL3C CF1319.
The offending vehicle was owned by Sh Mukesh ( respondent No.2/ owner) and was insured with M/S United Insurance Co Ltd (respondent no.3).

The petitioners have filed the present claim thereby claiming a sum of Rs. 2,00,00,000/ ( Two Crore ) from respondents as compensation, alongwith interest @ 18% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
3. The respondent No.1 and 2 have filed their W.S thereby stating that there is no cause of action to file the present petition.
It is submitted that in the present case the investigation has not been properly conducted by the Investigating officer.
It is submitted that the alleged eye witness of accident is false and procured witness.
4. The respondent no. 3 (insurance company) has filed a legal offer for a sum of Rs.12,23,566/ on the basis of documents being filed alongwith DAR and being filed by the petitioner.
The DAR has been clubbed with claim petition vide order dated 05.06.2018.

5. After completion of the proceedings, following issues are framed on 05.06,2018 as under:
(i) Whether Lakshya Verma sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated on 23.01.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL3CCF 1319 being driven by Respondent 1 Vishal and owned by Respondent No.2 Mukesh and insured by Respondent No.3 United India Insurance Co Ltd ?

OPP.

OPP.

6.
In order to prove their claim, petitioners have examined petitioner No.1 as PW1, PW2 Sh Sachin Kumar and Sh Deepankar Bhattacharya as PW3.
7. None of the respondents have led any evidence in support of their case.
8. I have heard ld. counsels appearing on behalf of petitioners and respondents.
I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submission and I also perused the record.

My issuewise findings are as under: ISSUE No.(i) Whether Lakshya Verma sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated on 23.01.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL3CCF1319 being driven by Respondent 1 Vishal and owned by Respondent No.2 Mukesh and insured by Respondent No.3 United India Insurance Co Ltd ?

OPP . 
9.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
To prove this fact petitioners examined PW3 Sh Deepankar Bhattacharya , who has deposed that on 23.01.2018, he was going towards Sector10, Dwarka New Delhi in his Scorpio car bearing No. DL10CG3148.
He was waiting at red light of Sector 313 Chowk.
He deposed that on turning into green signal he moved towards Ayushman Chowk, then a Swift Dzire Car over took his vehicle in high speed.

He has deposed at next red signal of Sector 412, Dwarka, near Dwarka International School, the said car in high speed and in rash and negligent manner hit a young boy, who was going on his bicycle towards Sector04 from Ayushman Chowk.

PW 3 has been duly crossexamined by all the respondents but the testimony of the said PW with respect to accident and rash & negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 could not be impeached.
Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing off a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/304A of IPC.
Though, respondent no.1 has not led any evidence.
Therefore, the evidence which has come on the file only can be considered and it becomes more relevant when there is no specific evidence led by other side in rebuttal.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that deceased cyclist was at fault, in any way.
10. The fact that Lakshya Verma died in that accident is also supported by his postmortem report on the dead body of victim.
After investigation, police indicted respondent no.1 for offences punishable under Sections 279/304A of IPC.
The charge sheet was filed against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his such implication.

Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of Car bearing No.DL3C CF1319 by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Lakshya Verma.
11.

This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Lakshya Verma died in a motor vehicle accident due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing No.DL3CCF1319 by respondent no.1.

6 ISSUE No.2: Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP.
12.
Petitioner no.1 and 2 are the mother and father of victim ( deceased Lakshay) as such LRs of victim.
They are entitled for claim.
13. Now coming to the extent of compensation.

According to the petitioners, at the time of accident,
the deceased Lakshya Verma was studying in Amity School of Engineering & Technology and pursuing B.Tech in II Semester.
He was aspiring singer and participated in so many music concerts such as 'Indian Idol' and musical show namely 'Magical Voice of India.

The deceased was pursuing the professional course and is a student of B Tech of II Semester and having a brilliant career and could have offer of employment after completion of his professional course.

Ld Counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the judgment of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd Vs Deo Pataudi, 2009 (8) Scale 194 where Hon'ble Supreme Court has assessed the monthly income of a deceased,who was pursuing B Tech as 25,000/ p.m for computation of compensation.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd Vs Deo Pataudi, 2009 (8) Scale 194
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The judgment relied upon by Ld Counsel for the petitioner is distinguishable on the facts as in that case the victim had almost completed his professional course and was having an employment offer from US based Company at the time of accident.
Here in the present case, there is no such circumstances.
But considering the fact that the deceased was having good academic record and was studying in Amity School of Engineering & Technology and pursuing B.Tech in II Semester.
So this Tribunal has assessed the monthly income of deceased as 19,000/ pm for computation of compensation.

14. As per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and future benefit have to be given @ 40%.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. Keeping in view the fact that the age of the deceased was 18 years old ( 15.01.2000, as per matriculation certificate ) The deceased was Bachelor at the time of accident so deceased spending 50% of his income on his personal expenses.
Therefore the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.13,300/ (19,000/ + 7,600/  13,300/) per month.
16. To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
A multiplier of 18 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 28,72,800/ (13,300/ x 12 x 18).
This amount of Rs. 28,72,800/ is allowed to petitioner no.1 and 2 as loss of dependency.

17. Apart from amount mentioned above, petitioner no. 1 is also granted a sum of Rs.17,000/ for funeral expenses, Rs.17,000/ for loss of estate and Rs. 44,000/ each to the petitioners for loss of consortium making a total sum of Rs. 29,94,800/

Detail of the whole award amount is: i. Loss of dependency Rs. 28,72,800/ ii. Funeral expenses Rs. 17,000/ iii. Loss of Estate Rs. 17,000/ v.
Loss of consortium (44,000/ each to Rs. 88,000/-
 the petitioners )

18.
Now coming to the extent of liability.
It has already been held herein above that the deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
He is primarily liable to make payment.
However, the petitioners have made the respondent no. 3 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no. 3 that it be directed to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
It is not in dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent no.3 on the date of accident.

This issue is decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that petitioners are entitled for compensation from respondent no.3.
ISSUE NO.2 (RELIEF)
19.
Petition in hands is allowed.

Respondent no.3 is directed to pay a sum of Rs. 29,94,800/
alongwith interest @ 7.5% to the petitioners as compensation in this case, within 30 days from today, from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 11.04.2018 till the date of compliance i.e.,
19.05.2023.
Amount of interim compensation (if any) be deducted from this amount.

The awarded amount shall remain as tax free in view of the judgment of Hon'ble High Court in case in R/Special Civil Application No.4800 of 2021 titled The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd Vs Chief Commissioner of Income Tax (TDS) decided on 05.04.2022.

14. As per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and future benefit have to be given @ 40%.
15. Keeping in view the fact that the age of the deceased was 18 years old ( 15.01.2000, as per matriculation certificate ) The deceased was Bachelor at the time of accident so deceased spending 50% of his income on his personal expenses.
Therefore the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.13,300/ (19,000/ + 7,600/  13,300/) per month.
16. To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
A multiplier of 18 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
However, the petitioners have made the respondent no. 3 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no. 3 that it be directed to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
